content.title: We found why you're exhausted
content.body: Your hemoglobin is 11.5 g/dL—below the normal range of 12.0-16.0. Your ferritin (iron stores) is also low at 9 ng/mL. This explains the persistent fatigue you've been feeling. The good news? Iron deficiency is one of the most fixable causes of low energy. Most people start feeling noticeably better within 2 to 4 weeks of addressing it.

content.title: Did you know?
content.body: You need 18mg of iron daily—nearly double what men need—to prevent anemia and fatigue. Yet 1 in 5 young Singaporean women are iron-deficient. Add iron-rich foods like spinach, lentils, or lean meat to your meals, and pair them with vitamin C for better absorption.

content.title: Boost your iron, boost your energy
content.body: Start rebuilding your iron stores with foods you can find at any hawker center or supermarket. Pair iron-rich foods with vitamin C (like citrus or tomatoes) to absorb more. Avoid tea or coffee with meals—they block iron absorption. You should start feeling the energy difference in 2 to 4 weeks.

content.title: Consider iron supplements with your doctor
content.body: With your ferritin at 9 ng/mL, food alone might take longer to replenish your iron stores. Iron supplements (like 50mg ferrous sulfate) can speed up recovery significantly. Ask your doctor about whether supplementation is right for you—they can recommend the best type and dosage for your situation.

content.title: There's a second energy drain: vitamin D
content.body: Your vitamin D level is 19 ng/mL—below the sufficient threshold of 30 ng/mL. Low vitamin D is associated with fatigue and low energy, so it's likely compounding your anemia. Singapore's indoor lifestyle (air-conditioned offices, minimal outdoor time) makes vitamin D insufficiency common despite our tropical sun. The fix is straightforward: sun exposure and supplementation.

metadata.rationale: m1 baseline - multi-factor connection using cognitive reframing. Secondary energy factor after anemia. Singapore context (indoor lifestyle) makes it relatable. Position 6 in build phase allows emotional recovery. Low complexity with clear prioritization (iron first).

content.title: 15 minutes of morning sun
content.body: Get 15 to 20 minutes of morning sunlight with your arms and legs exposed—this helps your body produce vitamin D naturally. Perfect timing for you: take a short walk before work (7-9am works great). For faster results, your doctor can recommend a vitamin D3 supplement (typically 1000-2000 IU daily). You should feel improvement in 4 to 6 weeks.
